facts.rationale: Distinguishes the caller's guard from the effects and exceptional behavior of the packet test.
facts.value: Performs one packet test and does no additional work if its result is -1; that test may itself have transport and buffer side effects. Otherwise it resets the returned buffer's cursor to zero, reads a command byte, processes values below 0x80, and releases values at or above 0x80. Buffer lookup and cursor/read results are unchecked. It retains no automatic local state between calls.

facts.rationale: Removes an unsupported inference about cleanup requirements while retaining the lifecycle role.
facts.value: Provides the serial-handler teardown hook invoked by TRKTerminateNub. This implementation performs no cleanup or state mutation and unconditionally returns kNoError; the no-op body does not establish that outstanding resources cannot exist.

evidence.why: Acquisition logic and unchecked exceptional paths.

facts.rationale: Preserves the acquisition purpose without promising safe rejection on all paths.
facts.value: Attempts to acquire one MetroTRK packet from UART availability into a message buffer, returning its identifier after a successful positive-count read of at most 0x880 bytes. Oversized input triggers bounded discard-read requests and an attempted kDSReplyNAK/error-6 reply. This implementation does not safely handle every unsuccessful acquisition path: allocation status is ignored and the cleanup identifier is uninitialized when polling reports a nonpositive count.

evidence.why: Producer, buffer writes, return sites and cleanup.
Allocation outputs on success and failure.

facts.rationale: Corrects universal cleanup wording and records the actual allocation output contract.
facts.value: TRKPollUART supplies a signed byte count. For a positive count, TRKGetFreeBuffer is called for an identifier and pointer, but its status is ignored. With successful allocation, a read of at most 0x880 bytes targets b->fData; kNoError causes b->fLength to be set and the identifier returned. Oversized counts drive repeated reads into the same data array, followed by TRKStandardACK(b, kDSReplyNAK, 6), which rewrites the buffer as a reply and attempts transmission. Remaining control flow tests id against -1, conditionally releases it, and returns -1. However, id has no initializer: nonpositive polling leaves it indeterminate, and allocation failure leaves b null and id untouched.

evidence.why: Guards, loop progress, ignored statuses and uninitialized identifier.

facts.rationale: Preserves exact acceptance conditions while distinguishing requested work from guaranteed transport outcomes.
facts.value: With successful allocation, a positive count no greater than 0x880 becomes a returned packet only when its UART read reports kNoError; a failed read reaches release and -1. Oversized input requests batches of min(remaining, 0x880), subtracting each requested batch regardless of read status, then attempts a NAK with numeric error 6 and releases the temporary buffer. Neither discard-read nor ACK status is checked, so complete draining and successful transmission are not guaranteed. Allocation failure is unchecked; a nonpositive poll reaches a comparison of uninitialized id. These source-level hazards prevent a defined no-packet/failure transition from being asserted for every call. No automatic local state is retained between calls.
